Maine’s 90-credit applied bachelor’s degrees: who they fit and what to check

Maine’s three approved 90-credit applied bachelor’s programs can suit some adults returning to college. The useful comparison is the work remaining after your records are evaluated, followed by whether the credential serves your employment and further-study goals.

Start with the three programs actually offered

The University of Maine System’s current announcement identifies three programs approved by the New England Commission of Higher Education in November 2025 and offered beginning fall 2026: Applied Psychology at the University of Maine at Presque Isle, Applied Business Management at the University of Maine at Fort Kent, and Applied Public Administration at the University of Maine at Augusta. Earlier proposals mentioned additional subjects; those proposals do not establish an available degree.

These are particular applied bachelor’s degrees designed for adult degree completion. They are not a rule reducing every Maine bachelor’s degree to 90 credits. Compare the exact award, delivery format, admission criteria and curriculum with a conventional degree before selecting one.

Three approved programs, with different curricula and eligibility checks. All amounts here are semester credits.
University and awardPublished structureAdmission or planning detail
UMPI Applied BA in Psychology90 credits: 40 general education, 45 psychology, at least 5 electivesYourPace adult-completion program; 30 UMPI credits required
UMFK Applied Business Management bachelor’s90 credits: 36 general education and 54 business; no free electives30 prior credits and adult-returner criteria; 30 UMFK credits required
UMA Applied BS in Public Administration90-credit applied degreeRelevant experience or prior learning, education-gap and GPA requirements; portfolio for work-based credit

Check that you qualify before comparing speed

UMPI describes its applied psychology option for adult completers with prior college credit or credit for prior learning who are returning after a pause of at least two years. UMFK publishes a 2.0 GPA requirement, at least 30 prior credits, and a two-year education gap, with an alternative route for community-college transfers who entered that college as adult completers. These conditions need an admissions review; simply being an adult does not establish eligibility.

UMA describes eligibility involving two years of relevant work experience or prior college or other learning, at least two years since the most recent college credits, and a 2.0 GPA. Work experience does not automatically become academic credit: the page requires a portfolio when seeking that award. Ask how the criteria apply to your education and employment history before paying for new preparatory courses.

A smaller degree still needs applicable credits

The system’s framework requires at least 30 credits at the campus awarding the degree. Against a 90-credit total, that leaves a mathematical maximum of 60 outside credits, or two thirds of the degree. It does not promise that 60 of your credits will apply. Major content, academic level, residency details and the institution’s rules for ACE and other prior learning remain separate checks.

This matters especially at UMFK, where the published curriculum has no free electives. A useful course must satisfy general education or business requirements rather than merely fit unused elective space. At UMPI, 45 psychology credits occupy half the degree. A large unrelated transcript can therefore leave more work than a smaller, closely matched one.

Request an evaluation against both the applied award and the longer alternative. Compare remaining courses, required campus credits, prerequisites and likely course availability. Buying a generic 60-credit outside basket before that evaluation risks spending money on courses with no remaining place.

Price the remaining work in the correct billing model

UMPI’s published 2026–27 undergraduate YourPace tuition is $1,800 per eight-week session. One, two and three paid sessions are tuition scenarios of $1,800, $3,600 and $5,400 before any other applicable charges or financial aid. These totals do not predict completion within those sessions; assessments, prerequisites, study time and feedback determine your pace.

Do not apply UMPI’s subscription price to UMA or UMFK. Request the current rate and fee schedule for the exact university, residency classification and program. UMA’s public applied-degree page includes a tuition total that does not reconcile with 90 credits at its displayed resident per-credit rate; obtain an individualized estimate rather than copying that advertised total.

Include the price of acquiring any missing outside credits, official records and any required university work. A 90-credit award may reduce requirements, but an already well-matched 120-credit degree can still be competitive after evaluation. The relevant budget is the remaining cost for your situation.

Ask future employers and graduate programs about the exact award

The universities explicitly warn that some employers and graduate programs require a 120-credit bachelor’s degree. NECHE approval establishes accreditation review of these offerings; it does not bind another institution’s admission policy or an employer’s qualification standard. Give a future graduate program the exact award title and 90-credit total and seek a written answer.

UMFK describes a pathway to its own master’s study when all admission requirements are met. That is not guaranteed admission or evidence about other graduate schools. UMPI also states that the psychology award does not qualify a graduate for clinical or counseling licensure. Professional practice requires its own preparation and jurisdiction-specific review.

Keep a route to the longer degree in view

UMPI describes a transition to its 120-credit psychology BA without losing the completed learning. UMA says every credit in the applied program carries into its full 121-credit public administration degree. Keep the actual 121-credit total in that comparison instead of rounding every conventional degree to 120.

Ask about the timing of that transition before accepting the shorter award. UMPI warns that earning the applied bachelor’s first can affect federal-aid availability when returning for the longer bachelor’s. Eligibility and funding should be resolved with the university, alongside the employment or graduate-school question.

Save your existing records, obtain the program-specific evaluations, and compare the resulting remaining-work lists. These programs are editorially researched options, not ready-made DegreeSteps course templates. Use the comparison tools to organize alternatives while the university determines the actual awards.

About this research

DegreeSteps editorial team · Degree planning and transfer-credit research

We explain educational choices using university catalogs, receiving-school course agreements, provider guidance, and the same researched degree models used by DegreeSteps. Our articles distinguish proposed coursework, original learning records, and individual university awards. Worked examples identify their program, format, units, and relevant dates. Founder stories are attributed as reported experience, without invented transcripts, savings totals, or reviewer credentials.
